Boole · Setup guides · Windows x64

Windows · x64 · CUDA, Vulkan, or CPU

Run a local AI model on Windows

Windows x64 can use a CUDA prebuilt, a Vulkan prebuilt, or the CPU prebuilt. Pick the package that matches the machine. The CLI does not ship a separate Windows arm64 GPU build on this page.

Requirements

  • 64-bit Windows on x64. Prebuilt packages: @node-llama-cpp/win-x64 (CPU), @node-llama-cpp/win-x64-cuda, @node-llama-cpp/win-x64-cuda-ext, and @node-llama-cpp/win-x64-vulkan.
  • Node.js 20 or newer.
  • For the CUDA prebuilts, the node-llama-cpp CUDA guide documents CUDA Toolkit 12.4+ or 13.1. That is the runtime’s requirement, not a speed Boole has measured on Windows.
  • Vulkan uses win-x64-vulkan. There is no Windows arm64 GPU package. ARM Windows is a separate guide, and it is CPU only.

boole doctor prints cuda or vulkan when that backend loads, and none on the CPU build. VRAM is printed only when getVramState returns it. The automatic size pick still uses RAM.

Install the Boole CLI

Node.js 20 or newer. Install the published package, or run it once with npx. This does not republish the package.

npm install -g @boole/cli
npx @boole/cli doctor

If node-llama-cpp is missing, boole run writes error: node-llama-cpp is not installed and npm install node-llama-cpp, then exits 1.

Check the machine with boole doctor

boole doctor prints the operating system, architecture, Node version, RAM total and available, the GPU backend (metal, cuda, vulkan, or none) and a device name when it has one. VRAM is printed only when getVramState returns it. It also prints the binaries and the cache path and size. All of that goes to standard error.

The verdict uses free RAM minus a 2 GiB headroom. It does not use VRAM. When that headroom leaves no room, it prints not enough memory for inference and exits 1.

boole doctor

Download a model with boole pull

Pass an alias, or repo:quant with a slash in the repo. --dir sets the cache. --yes skips the size question. --quiet suppresses the diagnostics.

The default cache is ~/Library/Caches/boole on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%\boole\cache on Windows, and $XDG_CACHE_HOME/boole or ~/.cache/boole elsewhere. BOOLE_CACHE overrides it.

A file reported over 2 GB asks [y/N] on a terminal unless you passed --yes. An interrupted download keeps a .partial file and resumes with an HTTP Range request.

The name is resolved on Hugging Face before the cache is checked. A file that is already on disk still causes that request. Saying no to the size prompt exits 0.

boole pull llama3
boole pull llama3 --yes
boole pull bartowski/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --yes

Run it with boole run

An alias such as llama3 picks a quant. A specifier with a slash and a colon, or a local .gguf path, is used as given. The prompt comes from --file, -p / --prompt, a second positional argument, or stdin. The first match wins.

Flags that change the run: --system / -s, --stream, --temp / -t (default 0.8), --ctx-size (default 2048), --max-tokens, --json, --jsonl, --yes, --quiet / -q. Standard output is the model text. Diagnostics stay on standard error.

The process calls getLlama({ gpu: 'auto' }) and loads the file. --gpu-layers is accepted by the parser and is not passed into loadModel in release 0.0.1. The CLI does not set a thread count.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 bad usage, 3 model unavailable (unknown name, missing quant, or not enough memory).

boole run llama3 -p "What does it mean to run a language model on the device?"
boole run ./weights.gguf -p "Hello"

Pick a model size for your RAM

Both doctor and an alias on run estimate a file size. They do not measure it. The formula in the hardware package is parameter count times bits per weight, divided by 8.

Bits per weight in that table: Q2_K 3.35, Q3_K_M 3.91, Q4_K_M 4.85, Q5_K_M 5.69, Q6_K 6.57, Q8_0 8.50. Usable memory is free RAM minus 2 GiB. The highest quant whose estimate fits is the one chosen. VRAM is displayed when the runtime reports it, and it is not an input to this pick.

doctor walks 1B, 3B, 7B, 8B, 13B, 34B, and 70B and keeps the largest size that fits. Those labels are the estimator’s ladder. They are not aliases, and they are not measured file sizes. For an 8B model at Q4_K_M the same formula comes out near 4.5 GiB. That is the estimate, not a file we weighed.

boole models lists the aliases. llama3 is 8B with Q3_K_M through Q8_0, and it has no Q2_K. llama3-70b is 70B with the same quants. phi3 is 3.8B (Q4_K_M through Q8_0) when memory is tight. mixtral is 47B with Q2_K through Q5_K_M. llama2 and codellama are 7B and do include Q2_K. Do not pass Q2_K for llama3.

boole models

Troubleshooting

node-llama-cpp is not installed

The error is exactly error: node-llama-cpp is not installed, then npm install node-llama-cpp. Exit code 1. Node 20 or newer is required before that install is useful.

Not enough memory

doctor exits 1 when free RAM is not above the 2 GiB headroom. run exits 3 when the alias’s smallest quant still does not fit, and it prints the estimate beside the memory it computed.

serve and list

boole serve and boole list print boole serve is not yet implemented or the same for list, and exit 1. They are not part of this setup.

CUDA does not load

Confirm the CUDA prebuilt installed, and that the toolkit matches the version the runtime’s CUDA guide documents. The CPU package win-x64 is the fallback this release actually ships. This page has no Windows tok/s number.
